possĭbĭlis , e, adj. possum,
I.that may exist or may be done, possible (post-Aug.): melius qui tertiam partem dixerunt δυνατόν, quod nostri possibile nominant, Quint. 3, 8, 25: “condiciones,” Dig. 28, 3, 16 : possibile est, with subject-clause, ib. 25, 2, 3; Vulg. 2 Macc. 3, 6.—Hence, adv.: possĭ-bĭlĭter , Jul. ap. Aug. c. Sec. Resp. Jul. 2, 52.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
